title: The Zenos E10 Returns with Lotus’ Help

body_markdown:
You may remember the Zenos E10 from its exploits on *The Grand Tour,* when James May pitted it against Richard Hammond in a Mazda Miata and Jeremy Clarkson in an Alfa Romeo 4C.


Racing around the former *Game of Thrones* set in Morocco was probably the little car’s finest hour, for not long afterwards the company closed shop.


Almost a decade later, there’s *good news* , as Clarkson would say, because Zenos is back and reviving the E10 with what it describes as “a raft of enhancements.”


It looks essentially the same, but there’s new lighting, and side skirts to aid aerodynamics. The bug-like bodywork is all carbon fiber, and there’s a central carbon tub, with extruded aluminium subframes bolted to it. The front suspension deploys race-ready pushrods, while more conventional coilovers are used at the rear.


Zenos


The Zenos E10 comes in two versions: the r2 packs a 2.3-liter, 296-hp turbocharged four-cylinder engine, while the rZ gets a 2.0-liter turbo and 375 horses. In either case, the engine is mid-mounted and drives the rear wheels via a six-speed manual transmission. They’re both fearsomely fast, of course, with the r2 clocking zero-to-62 mph in 3.8 seconds and the rZ cutting that to 3.2 seconds. Top speed is a breezy 150 mph.


The interior is as basic as they come, with figure-hugging carbon race seats and instruments provided by an AIMS PMU race dashboard. Buyers can opt for a full windscreen or a wind deflector for track use.


For buyers outside of the U.K., it’s being sold as a track car only, but bonkers Brit owners will be able to road-register the Zenos after shelling out around $155,000 for the r2 or $173,000 for the rZ model.


Rather than attempting to revive the original factory, or building a new one, Zenos has signed a deal with Lotus to have the cars built at the Hethel Performance Hub. Deliveries begin in 2027.
